what_its_for: Interferon gamma-1b is used to help prevent serious infections in people with a condition called chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), which is an inherited immune system disorder. It is also used to slow down the worsening of a serious lung condition called severe, malignant osteopetrosis. This medicine works by boosting your immune system to help your body fight off infections and disease.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your upper arm, thigh, or stomach area. A healthcare provider will teach you or a caregiver how to properly prepare and give the injection at home. Always rotate the injection site each time to avoid skin irritation. Use a new needle and syringe for every injection. Do not shake the vial — gently swirl it if needed. Always check the liquid before injecting; do not use it if it looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it.
dosing: Your doctor will determine the right dose based on your body surface area (a calculation using your height and weight). The typical dose is 50 micrograms per square meter (mcg/m²) or 1.5 million units per square meter, given three times per week (for example, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday). Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to your next scheduled dose. Do not give two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Try to keep a consistent schedule of three injections per week.
storage: Store unopened vials in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze this medication — throw it away if it has been frozen. Keep vials in their original carton to protect them from light. Do not leave the medicine at room temperature for longer than 12 hours; if it has been out of the refrigerator for more than 12 hours, throw it away. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children. Dispose of used needles and syringes in an approved sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting vaccines (especially live vaccines) without first talking to your doctor, as interferon gamma-1b may affect how your immune system responds. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or unusually tired. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it may worsen certain side effects like dizziness or fatigue. Tell all of your healthcare providers that you are taking this medication before starting any new medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a high fever or chills (especially within a few hours of your injection), chest pain or tightness, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, confusion, unusual behavior changes, or severe dizziness. Also contact your doctor if you notice: signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing), numbness or tingling, unusual bleeding or bruising, signs of liver problems (yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, stomach pain), or new or worsening neurological symptoms. Also let your doctor know about any persistent or bothersome side effects such as ongoing flu-like symptoms, injection site reactions, nausea, or vomiting.
when_it_works: This medication works continuously to help keep your immune system stronger and reduce the risk of serious infections. You may not feel a noticeable difference right away, but it is working in the background to protect you. It is very important to keep using it regularly as prescribed, even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits of using this medicine during pregnancy or breastfeeding should be carefully discussed with your doctor. Children: This medication is used in children with chronic granulomatous disease; dosing is carefully adjusted by weight and body size. Elderly patients: Use with caution; older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as confusion or heart and nervous system effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how your body handles the medication and may require closer monitoring.
